key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow can efficiently map thermodynamic stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloy compositions and reveal where stable mixtures actually exist.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical screening tool for designing more stable Pb- and Sn-based perovskite solar absorbers by identifying composition ranges with the best phase stability.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials were trained on DFT data to relax alloy structures efficiently.
Secondary machine-learning models predicted energies directly from unrelaxed structures.
The workflow computed free-energy landscapes across compositions and phases while capturing alloy disorder and FA molecular orientations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports free-energy landscape calculations for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, showing narrower stable regions in Sn-based alloys and maximum stability at high iodide content.
watch_item: The approach depends on ML model fidelity and may be less reliable in poorly sampled composition or phase regions, especially near complex disorder-driven boundaries.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
